Gauss-Markov assumptions(MLR.1-MLR.5)




MLR.1 (Linear in Parameters)
    y = β0 + β1x1 + β2x2 + · · · + βkxk + u
MLR.2 (Random Sampling)
     (xi1, xi2, · · · , xik, yi) : i = 1, 2, · · · , n are i.i.d

     E(ui|xi1, xi2, · · · , xik) = 0

P-value

Confidence interval




    Confidence interval is an interval estimated around a sample mean under a
     pre-specified confidence level (1 −α) that provides a range within which
     the true population mean is expected to lie.

    Commonly used confidence levels are 99%, 95%, 90%.

Statistical Inference    Testing multiple linear restrictions: The F test

Unrestricted model vs restricted model



For an unrestricted model:

                     y = β0 + β1x1 + β2x2 + β3x3 + u

We impose the null hypothesis with three exclusion restrictions:

                   H0 : β1 = 0, β2 = 0, β3 = 0

against
                      H1 : H0 is not true

Then, we have the restricted model:

                y = β0 + 0 · x1 + 0 · x2 + 0 · x3 + u = β0 + u

Statistical Inference    Testing multiple linear restrictions: The F test

Joint hypotheses test: F-test

    F test is a statistical test that is used in hypothesis testing to check whether
     the variances of two populations or two samples are equal or not.

    F statistic for testing multiple restrictions:

     Rejection rule: F > Fα(q, n −k −1)
